title: Secret-Shaped Member Names
description: One shared definition of secret-shaped member names and credential-shaped string values. Families that must never carry a secret reference noSecretMembers on an object, or the individual definitions. secret-keys.conformance.json lists names and values every regex engine must classify the same way; change the patterns and the table together, here only.

secretShapedName.description: Matches member names that name a secret value: value, secret(s), token(s), password, passwd, passphrase, pem, bearer, credential(s), auth, privkey, and compounds such as private key, api key, access token, refresh token, client secret, access key, secret key, session token, auth token; as the whole name, after a separator, or as a camelCase suffix. Uses character classes only (no inline flags, no lookaround) so ECMA-262, Python re and Rust regex agree. Apply only to names that satisfy memberName.

noSecretMembers.description: Applied to an object: every member name is a memberName and none is secret-shaped.

memberName.description: Member names a contract may use: ASCII letters, digits, underscore, dot, hyphen. Written as 'contains no other character' rather than an anchored pattern, because engines disagree on whether $ matches before a trailing newline. With the alphabet fixed, no line terminator can reach secretShapedName.

credentialShapedValue.description: Matches string values that carry a recognisable credential: a bearer token, GitHub token, sk- API key, AWS access key id, PEM private key, age secret key, or JWT. A match means a secret was pasted; no match proves nothing, so this is a backstop, not a guarantee. Character classes only, no lookaround.
